newsitem.title: USA: Littlefield Adams faces doubt about future.
newsitem.headline: Littlefield Adams faces doubt about future.

text.p: Littlefield, Adams & Co said its limited financial resources and dependence on sales of Harley-Davidson Inc licensed products have raised substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern.
It also said it did not satisfy all the requirements needed for listing on the American Stock Exchange and there could be no assurances the listing would continue.
Independent auditors Arthur Andersen LLP included a discussion relating to Littlefield's ability to continue as a growing concern in its 1996 audit opinion, the company said.
Sales of licensed Harley products accounded for 90 percent of the company's 1996 net product sales, it said. The license expired on December 31, the company said.

In its most recent fourth quarter, the company said revenues increased mostly because of efforts to sell its inventory of licensed Harley products before the license expired. The company reported an earnings loss of $0.09 per share compared to a loss of $0.31 per share in the prior year's fourth quarter.

Littlefied, Adams, which made a similar announcement about its ability to continue as a growing concern when it released fourth quarter earnings last year, said it was still trying to enhance and stabilize its businesses through the acquisition of significant new licenses, the development of new product lines and the reduction of overhead.
